Rating notch calculator + country rating change indicator (Watchlist POC slice)

Source: POC_Requirements_v0.2_EN.md (Corporate Client Credit Monitoring — Watchlist Tool).
This job is a 2-requirement slice of that document. Build only these two requirements.

## Requirements (verbatim from the POC)

| Req ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria (summary) |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-06-02 | A notch calculator helper shall be available: analyst selects previous rating and current rating → system outputs notch change and resultant WL | BBB+ → BB+ = 2 notch downgrade → WL=1 displayed |
| REQ-03-12 | Indicator 12 (Country rating change): Pre-filled from public source; notch change auto-calculated | 1 notch → WL=1; 2+ notches → WL=2; auto-filled value editable |

Related rule (REQ-03-13, Indicator 13 — external rating change): 2 notch downgrade → WL=1; 3+ notches → WL=2.

## Clarifications for this slice (confirmed by the business unit)

- C1. Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-.
  A notch is one step on this scale. Input is trimmed and case-insensitive ("bbb+" = "BBB+"); anything else is rejected with a RangeError.
- C2. The POC example for REQ-06-02 miscounts: BBB+ → BB+ is 3 notches (BBB+ → BBB → BBB- → BB+). The calculator's WL uses the
  Indicator 13 thresholds (2 notches → WL=1, 3+ → WL=2), so BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade → WL=2, and BBB+ → BBB- = 2 notches → WL=1.
- C3. Upgrades and unchanged ratings → WL=0 for both indicators.
- C4. Fetching the rating from a public source is OUT of scope for this slice; the indicator takes the previous and current rating as input.
- C6. A 1-notch downgrade gives calculator WL 0 (Indicator 13 starts at 2 notches); Indicator 12 is unaffected (1 notch → WL 1).
- C7. "Auto-filled value editable" (REQ-03-12) is met by the contract: the caller passes whichever previous/current rating the
  analyst confirmed or edited. No override parameter, no persistence and no audit trail in this slice.
- C8. "Displayed" (REQ-06-02) is met by the returned `{ notches, direction, wl }`: the screens of the POC are built later
  by other parts and render this value. No UI, CLI or printed output in this slice.

## Contract (other parts of the POC will import exactly these)

- `src/ratings/notch.mjs`
  - `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer; positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged.
  - `notchCalculator(previous, current)` → `{ notches, direction: "downgrade" | "upgrade" | "unchanged", wl }` (wl per C2/C3).
- `src/indicators/countryRating.mjs`
  - `countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current)` → 0 | 1 | 2 (REQ-03-12 thresholds, C3), built on `notchChange`.

Plain Node ESM, no dependencies; tests with `node --test` next to the code under `test/`.

# Role catalog — Michael selects roles ONLY from this list (not from all of ECC's agents).
# `dl roles` turns the selected roles into project-specific role cards (.work/<job>/roles/<role>.md); on the Munder
# Difflin floor every seat of a role is a person (dl md-hire). A role card = rules.all + rules.<kind> + the role's own
# rules + project facts.
#
# Format (kept to a small YAML subset so bin/roles.mjs can read it without dependencies):
#   2-space indentation · `key: value` · `- item` lists · "double-quoted" or bare scalars · `#` comments
#
# kind:     ba | lead | dev | review | qa      (Michael himself is the PM/orchestrator)
# agent:    subagent type to call. "ecc:"-prefixed ones come from the ECC plugin.
# writes:   can it write files? (ECC architect/reviewers are read-only — on purpose)
# when:     selection rule (Michael decides at intake from the request + the repo)
# always:   selected for every job
# floor:    Munder Difflin look (character + accent) when the role runs on the office floor

rules:
  all:
    - "You work on exactly one job. Your input is the prompt you were given plus the files it names; nothing else is assumed."
    - "Never run state-changing dl commands (new, phase, roles, wt, card, gate, qa, review, integrate, ship, learn, cleanup). Michael owns the flow."
    - "Push only your own card branch (never main/master, never the job branch, never force); never delete .work/ or job/* branches; never write in the main checkout."
    - "Answer in exactly the output format the prompt asks for. Put details in files (handoff, plan), not in your reply."
    - "If something is unclear and it changes scope, say so under open questions / open issues. Do not guess scope."
  ba:
    - "Analysis only: do not write code or tests and do not modify files. Return the plan, the card specs or the closing check as text."
    - "Every acceptance criterion is numbered (AC-1, AC-2, …), traces to a requirement ID or a stated clarification, and is a Given/When/Then with concrete values."
    - "Cover the edges: boundaries, invalid input, error paths, empty values — say what must happen."
    - "Write Out of scope explicitly. Ask only open questions whose answer changes the scope."
    - "When the request contradicts itself, name the contradiction and the resolution you assume."
    - "A card spec covers every AC the card claims and nothing outside the card's scope."
  lead:
    - "Do not write code or modify files. Produce cards only."
    - "One card = one agent can finish it in one session. Split anything bigger."
    - "scope = narrow repo-relative globs for the dev: the code and its unit tests. Never '**', never paths outside the repo."
    - "verify = a command, run from the worktree root, that runs THIS card's unit tests, not the whole suite."
    - "qa_scope = where the QA role writes the card's integration/e2e tests (e.g. test/integration/<area>/**), separate from scope; qa_verify = the command that runs them."
    - "context must let a developer who never saw the plan do the card: why, files, decisions, contracts."
    - "Cards that touch the same files must be ordered with depends_on; parallel cards never share scope."
  dev:
    - "Work only inside the card worktree you were given. Every path is relative to it."
    - "Change only files matching the card's scope. Out-of-scope needs go under 'Open issues' in the handoff."
    - "TDD: for every behaviour write the unit test first, see it fail, implement, see it pass, refactor. Unit tests live in your scope, next to the code's test folder."
    - "Never write or change files in the card's qa_scope — those are the QA role's integration/e2e tests. After a QA round they must pass unchanged."
    - "Done means: the card's verify command (your unit tests) passes in the worktree, everything is committed ('<CARD-ID>: <title>'), the handoff is filled."
    - "Push only your card branch; no merge (except 'git merge <job branch>' when told to resolve a conflict), no branch switching, no amending others' commits."
    - "On a retry, resolve every feedback item first and mention each one in the handoff."
  review:
    - "Review only; do not modify files."
    - "Judge the change against the card: acceptance criteria met, correctness, security, test quality, scope."
    - "'changes' only for blocking defects (an AC not met, a bug, a security hole, missing tests, out-of-scope edits). Style goes to nits."
    - "Every blocking item names file, line, issue and the fix."
  qa:
    - "Write the card's integration and/or end-to-end tests — at least one per acceptance criterion of the spec, named after it, using the spec's test data."
    - "Write only inside the card's qa_scope. Never change product code or the dev's unit tests."
    - "Test through the public surface (exported API, endpoint, CLI, UI flow), the way the rest of the system or a user uses it."
    - "Run qa_verify, commit only your tests ('<CARD-ID> QA: …'), leave the worktree clean."
    - "If a criterion fails, keep the failing test committed as evidence and report it — do not fix the code."
    - "Every AC gets a verdict, pass or fail, with the test that shows it."

roles:
  ba:
    kind: ba
    agent: business-analyst
    writes: false
    always: true
    does: "Turns the request into a traceable plan (Given/When/Then ACs), writes a spec for every card, checks the ACs at closing."
    floor:
      character: pam
      accent: mint

  tech-lead:
    kind: lead
    agent: ecc:architect
    writes: false
    when: "New module, API/schema/data-model change, work touching 2+ areas, or 4+ cards expected"
    does: "Technical approach + cross-area contracts (API schema, types). Produces cards."
    rules:
      - "Write cross-area contracts (API shapes, shared types) into the context of every card that uses them."
    floor:
      character: jim
      accent: sky

  backend-lead:
    kind: lead
    agent: ecc:architect
    focus: backend
    when: "Any API, service, DB, queue, domain logic or integration work"
    does: "Produces backend cards; later reviews backend cards (together with the stack reviewer)."
    rules:
      - "Put schema changes and their migrations in the same card; data-changing migrations must be reversible."
    floor:
      character: oscar
      accent: amber

  frontend-lead:
    kind: lead
    agent: ecc:architect
    focus: frontend
    when: "Any web UI, component, state or routing work"
    does: "Produces frontend cards; later reviews them."
    rules:
      - "Reuse existing components and design tokens; name them in the card context."
    floor:
      character: kelly
      accent: rose

  mobile-lead:
    kind: lead
    agent: ecc:architect
    focus: mobile
    when: "Any Android/iOS app work"
    does: "Produces mobile cards; later reviews them."
    rules:
      - "Cards that need a device say so in their context; they run one at a time per device."
    floor:
      character: ryan
      accent: violet

  backend:
    kind: dev
    agent: backend-dev
    writes: true
    when: "backend-lead was selected"
    rules:
      - "Keep public contracts (exports, endpoints, response shapes) exactly as the card states them."
      - "Validate external input at the boundary; no secrets in code or tests."
    floor:
      character: dwight
      accent: amber

  frontend:
    kind: dev
    agent: frontend-dev
    writes: true
    when: "frontend-lead was selected"
    rules:
      - "Use the existing components, tokens and data-fetching pattern; no new UI library."

    floor:
      character: phyllis
      accent: rose

    floor:
      character: kevin
      accent: violet

  database:
    kind: dev
    agent: database-dev
    writes: true
    when: "The database is owned separately: schema, migrations and data changes go through their own cards (readiness ARC-data / architecture has a db component)"
    rules:
      - "Every schema change ships with a forward migration and, where data allows, a tested rollback."
      - "Migrations are backward compatible with the code currently deployed (expand → migrate → contract)."
    floor:
      character: stanley
      accent: slate

  security:
    kind: review
    agent: ecc:security-reviewer
    writes: false
    when: "auth, permissions, payments, personal data, secrets, file upload, handling external input"
    does: "Reviews the relevant cards IN ADDITION to the stack reviewer."
    rules:
      - "Check OWASP Top 10 classes relevant to the change, secrets, authz on every new entry point."
    floor:
      character: creed
      accent: slate

  qa:
    kind: qa
    agent: qa-tester
    writes: false
    always: true
    does: "Writes and runs each card's integration/e2e tests for its acceptance criteria (after the gate, before the Lead review)."
    floor:
      character: angela
      accent: mint

  a11y:
    kind: review
    agent: ecc:a11y-architect
    writes: false
    when: "readiness UX-a11y is decided (there is an accessibility target)"
    does: "Reviews UI cards against the decided accessibility target, in addition to the stack reviewer."
    rules:
      - "Check the decided target (e.g. WCAG 2.1 AA) on every UI element the card adds or changes: names, roles, focus, contrast, motion."

  performance:
    kind: review
    agent: ecc:performance-optimizer
    writes: false
    when: "readiness NFR-performance is decided (there are latency/throughput/volume targets)"
    does: "Reviews cards on performance-critical paths against the decided targets."
    rules:
      - "Judge against the decided numbers, with evidence (a measurement, a complexity argument) — not taste."

  quality:
    kind: review
    agent: ecc:silent-failure-hunter
    writes: false
    when: "Error handling or failure paths are central to the change (payments, integrations, data loss risk)"
    does: "Looks for swallowed errors, silent fallbacks and missing failure paths, in addition to the stack reviewer."

  docs:
    kind: dev
    agent: ecc:doc-updater
    writes: true
    when: "readiness DEL-docs is decided (documentation, changelog or runbook updates are required)"
    does: "Writes the documentation cards (README, API docs, changelog, runbooks) in the docs component."
    rules:
      - "Document what was built and decided (plan, readiness, report) — nothing speculative."

  qa-web:
    kind: qa
    agent: ecc:e2e-runner
    writes: true
    when: "A web user flow changes"
    does: "Runs end-to-end checks on the integrated job branch; durable e2e tests go through a card."
    floor:

    when: "A mobile user flow changes and a device/emulator is connected"
    does: "Michael drives ARTEMIS himself (mobile_run_task); a separate mobile-dev card is opened for durable test code."

# `dl roles` turns the selected roles into project-specific role cards (.work/<job>/roles/<role>.md); on the Munder

# rules + project facts.
#
# Format (kept to a small YAML subset so bin/roles.mjs can read it without dependencies):
#   2-space indentation · `key: value` · `- item` lists · "double-quoted" or bare scalars · `#` comments
#
# kind:     ba | lead | dev | review | qa      (Michael himself is the PM/orchestrator)
# agent:    subagent type to call. "ecc:"-prefixed ones come from the ECC plugin.
# writes:   can it write files? (ECC architect/reviewers are read-only — on purpose)
# when:     selection rule (Michael decides at intake from the request + the repo)
# always:   selected for every job
# floor:    Munder Difflin look (character + accent) when the role runs on the office floor

rules:
  all:
    - "You work on exactly one job. Your input is the prompt you were given plus the files it names; nothing else is assumed."
    - "Never run state-changing dl commands (new, phase, roles, wt, card, gate, qa, review, integrate, ship, learn, cleanup). Michael owns the flow."
    - "Push only your own card branch (never main/master, never the job branch, never force); never delete .work/ or job/* branches; never write in the main checkout."
    - "Answer in exactly the output format the prompt asks for. Put details in files (handoff, plan), not in your reply."
    - "If something is unclear and it changes scope, say so under open questions / open issues. Do not guess scope."
  ba:
    - "Analysis only: do not write code or tests and do not modify files. Return the plan, the card specs or the closing check as text."
    - "Every acceptance criterion is numbered (AC-1, AC-2, …), traces to a requirement ID or a stated clarification, and is a Given/When/Then with concrete values."
    - "Cover the edges: boundaries, invalid input, error paths, empty values — say what must happen."
    - "Write Out of scope explicitly. Ask only open questions whose answer changes the scope."
    - "When the request contradicts itself, name the contradiction and the resolution you assume."
    - "A card spec covers every AC the card claims and nothing outside the card's scope."
  lead:
    - "Do not write code or modify files. Produce cards only."
    - "One card = one agent can finish it in one session. Split anything bigger."
    - "scope = narrow repo-relative globs for the dev: the code and its unit tests. Never '**', never paths outside the repo."
    - "verify = a command, run from the worktree root, that runs THIS card's unit tests, not the whole suite."
    - "qa_scope = where the QA role writes the card's integration/e2e tests (e.g. test/integration/<area>/**), separate from scope; qa_verify = the command that runs them."
    - "context must let a developer who never saw the plan do the card: why, files, decisions, contracts."
    - "Cards that touch the same files must be ordered with depends_on; parallel cards never share scope."
  dev:
    - "Work only inside the card worktree you were given. Every path is relative to it."
    - "Change only files matching the card's scope. Out-of-scope needs go under 'Open issues' in the handoff."
    - "TDD: for every behaviour write the unit test first, see it fail, implement, see it pass, refactor. Unit tests live in your scope, next to the code's test folder."
    - "Never write or change files in the card's qa_scope — those are the QA role's integration/e2e tests. After a QA round they must pass unchanged."
    - "Done means: the card's verify command (your unit tests) passes in the worktree, everything is committed ('<CARD-ID>: <title>'), the handoff is filled."
    - "Push only your card branch; no merge (except 'git merge <job branch>' when told to resolve a conflict), no branch switching, no amending others' commits."
    - "On a retry, resolve every feedback item first and mention each one in the handoff."
  review:
    - "Review only; do not modify files."
    - "Judge the change against the card: acceptance criteria met, correctness, security, test quality, scope."
    - "'changes' only for blocking defects (an AC not met, a bug, a security hole, missing tests, out-of-scope edits). Style goes to nits."
    - "Every blocking item names file, line, issue and the fix."
  qa:
    - "Write the card's integration and/or end-to-end tests — at least one per acceptance criterion of the spec, named after it, using the spec's test data."
    - "Write only inside the card's qa_scope. Never change product code or the dev's unit tests."
    - "Test through the public surface (exported API, endpoint, CLI, UI flow), the way the rest of the system or a user uses it."
    - "Run qa_verify, commit only your tests ('<CARD-ID> QA: …'), leave the worktree clean."
    - "If a criterion fails, keep the failing test committed as evidence and report it — do not fix the code."
    - "Every AC gets a verdict, pass or fail, with the test that shows it."

    floor:
      character: ryan

    agent: backend-dev
    writes: true
